source_refs.note: Book p. 223-224: 12.2.3 Limit at Infinity: (a) limit as x -> +inf (lim 1/x = 0), (b) limit as x -> -inf, Theorem lim a/x^p = 0 (p positive rational) with 'For example' (p. 224).

blocks.text: Ab tak humne limits ko is tarah dekha ke \(x\) kisi number \(c\) ki taraf ja raha hai, jaise \(x \to 2\) ya \(x \to 0\). Ab ek naya sawal: agar \(x\) kisi number ki taraf na jaye balke barhta hi chala jaye, beghair kisi had ke, to function ka kya hota hai? Isi ko limit at infinity (la-mehdood par limit) kehte hain. Yeh section aglay do sections (12.2.4 aur 12.2.5) ki buniyad hai, is liye ise dhyan se parhiye.

Kitab kehti hai: hum functions \(f(x)\), \(f(x)g(x)\) aur \(\frac{f(x)}{g(x)}\) ki limits parh chuke hain jab \(x \to c\) (koi number). Ab dekhte hain ke function \(f(x)\) ki limit ka kya hota hai agar \(c\) ki jagah \(+\infty\) ya \(-\infty\) ho (limits at infinity), yani jab \(x \to +\infty\) aur \(x \to -\infty\).

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text:
Sab se pehle ek ahem baat: \(\infty\) (infinity) koi number nahin hai. Hum kabhi \(x = \infty\) nahin rakh sakte.
"\(x \to +\infty\)" ka matlab hai ke \(x\) bari se bari positive values leta jata hai (10, 100, 1000, ...) aur kahin rukta nahin.
"\(x \to -\infty\)" ka matlab hai ke \(x\) negative values leta hai jin ka size barhta jata hai (\(-10, -100, -1000, \dots\)).
Sawal sirf yeh hai: jab \(x\) us simt (direction) mein door chala jaye, to kya \(f(x)\) kisi ek fixed number ke paas aa kar tik jata hai? Agar haan, to wohi number limit hai.

Maan lijiye \(f(x) = \frac{1}{x}\), jab \(x \ne 0\). Is function ki khoobi yeh hai ke jab \(x\) kaafi bara ho to \(f(x)\) ki value ko zero ke jitna chahein utna qareeb laya ja sakta hai. Is baat ko hum yun likhte hain:

blocks.text_alt: limit as x tends to infinity of 1 over x equals 0

blocks.caption: Humari table (kitab mein nahin): x jitna bara, 1/x utna zero ke qareeb, magar kabhi zero nahin.

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text:
Table ko ghor se dekhiye: har dafa \(x\) ko 10 se zarb dene par \(\frac{1}{x}\) das guna chhota ho jata hai.
Rozmarra ki misaal: ek roti ko 10 logon mein baantein to har ek ko \(\frac{1}{10}\) milti hai; 1000 logon mein baantein to sirf \(\frac{1}{1000}\), yani na hone ke barabar. Log jitne barhte jayen, har ek ka hissa zero ke qareeb hota jata hai, magar bilkul zero kabhi nahin hota.
"Jitna chahein utna qareeb" ka matlab yeh hai: aap zero se koi bhi chhota faasla bata dein, jaise 0.000001; kaafi bara \(x\) (yahan \(x > 10^{6}\)) le kar \(\frac{1}{x}\) ko us se bhi zyada qareeb laya ja sakta hai.
Dhyan dein: limit woh value hai jis ki taraf function ja raha hai, zaroori nahin ke function us tak pohanche.
Kitab kehti hai ke is qisam ki limits bilkul usi tarah handle hoti hain jaise \(x \to +\infty\) wali, yani

blocks.text_alt: limit as x tends to minus infinity of 1 over x equals 0, where x is not 0

blocks.caption: Humari table (kitab mein nahin): bare negative x ke liye 1/x ek chhota negative number hai jo zero ki taraf jata hai.

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text: Farq sirf sign ka hai: \(x\) negative ho to \(\frac{1}{x}\) bhi negative hai, magar us ka size phir bhi chhota hota jata hai: \(-0.1, -0.01, -0.001\). Yeh numbers neeche (left) ki taraf se zero ke qareeb aa rahe hain, aur limit phir bhi 0 hai.
Agla theorem limits at infinity nikalne mein bohat kaam aata hai.
Theorem: Maan lijiye \(p\) ek positive rational number hai. Agar \(x^{p}\) defined ho (yani us ki value real number mein exist kare), to

blocks.text_alt: limit as x tends to plus infinity of a over x to the power p equals 0
limit as x tends to minus infinity of a over x to the power p equals 0

blocks.text: jahan \(a\) koi bhi real number hai.

Misaal ke taur par (kitab ki misaalein),
\[\lim_{x\to \pm\infty}\dfrac{6}{x^{3}} = 0\]
\[\lim_{x\to +\infty}\dfrac{-5}{\sqrt[5]{x}} = 0\]

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text:
Yeh theorem sahi kyun hai? Upar \(a\) fixed hai, woh badalta nahin. Neeche \(x^{p}\) ka size \(p > 0\) ki wajah se barhta hi chala jata hai. Ek fixed number ko bare se bare number se divide karein to jawab zero ke qareeb hota jata hai, bilkul roti wali misaal ki tarah.
"Agar \(x^{p}\) defined ho" ki shart kyun? \(x \to -\infty\) mein kuch powers exist hi nahin karti. Misaal: \(x^{1/2} = \sqrt{x}\) negative \(x\) ke liye real number nahin, is liye \(\lim_{x\to -\infty}\frac{a}{\sqrt{x}}\) ka koi matlab nahin. Lekin odd roots, jaise \(\sqrt[3]{x}\) ya \(\sqrt[5]{x}\), negative \(x\) ke liye bhi defined hain.
Kitab ki misaalon mein: pehli mein \(a = 6\), \(p = 3\); doosri mein \(a = -5\), \(p = \frac{1}{5}\), kyun ke \(\sqrt[5]{x} = x^{1/5}\).

blocks.title: Hamari taraf se misaal
blocks.text:
Yeh misaal humari taraf se hai: \(\lim_{x\to -\infty}\frac{7}{x^{2}}\).
Yahan \(a = 7\), \(p = 2\), aur \(x^{2}\) har \(x\) ke liye defined hai. To theorem se limit \(= 0\).
Tasdeeq: \(x = -100\) par \(\frac{7}{10000} = 0.0007\), jo zero ke bohat qareeb hai.

blocks.title: Khud sochiye
blocks.text:
Kya \(\lim_{x\to +\infty}\frac{3}{\sqrt{x}} = 0\)? Aur \(\lim_{x\to -\infty}\frac{3}{\sqrt{x}}\)?
Jawab: pehli limit 0 hai (\(p = \frac{1}{2}\), positive \(x\) ke liye \(\sqrt{x}\) defined). Doosri ka koi matlab nahin, kyun ke negative \(x\) ke liye \(\sqrt{x}\) real nahin.

blocks.title: Exam tip
blocks.text: Yeh theorem 12.2.5 wale method ki jaan hai. Jab bhi aap \(\frac{10}{x} \to 0\) ya \(\frac{50}{x^{3}} \to 0\) likhte hain, aap yahi theorem istemal kar rahe hote hain. Paper mein wajah ke taur par "\(\because \lim \frac{a}{x^{p}} = 0\)" likh dein, poore marks milenge.

blocks.title: Yaad rakhne wali baatein
blocks.text:
1. \(\infty\) number nahin; \(x \to \pm\infty\) ka matlab hai \(x\) ka size beghair had ke barhna, positive ya negative simt mein.
2. \(\lim_{x\to \pm\infty}\frac{1}{x} = 0\).
3. Theorem: \(\lim_{x\to \pm\infty}\frac{a}{x^{p}} = 0\), har real \(a\) aur positive rational \(p\) ke liye, jab \(x^{p}\) defined ho.
4. Limit woh value hai jis ki taraf function jata hai; zaroori nahin ke function us tak pohanche.

blocks.title: Aam ghaltiyan
blocks.text:
1. \(x = \infty\) ko number samajh kar rakh dena aur jawab \(\frac{1}{\infty}\) likh dena. Jawab limit hai, yani 0.
2. Yeh samajhna ke \(\frac{a}{x^{p}}\) ka jawab \(a\) ya \(\infty\) hoga. Upar fixed hai aur neeche barh raha hai, is liye fraction zero ki taraf jata hai.
3. \(x \to -\infty\) ke saath even root, jaise \(\sqrt{x}\), par theorem laga dena, jab ke negative \(x\) ke liye woh defined hi nahin.
